description: This file defines the internal sealed partial class 'Catalog' within the Orleans.Runtime namespace. It manages grain activations, including creation, deactivation, registration, unregistration, and handling silo status changes. It interacts with various components such as activation directories, grain directory resolvers, and silo status oracles, and includes logging and instrumentation for activation lifecycle events.

classes.name: Catalog
classes.description: Manages grain activations within a silo, including creation, deactivation, registration, unregistration, and handling silo status changes. Implements lifecycle participation and interacts with various components for activation lifecycle management.

methods.name: UnregisterMessageTarget
methods.description: Unregisters a message target (activation) and stops message delivery to it.

methods.name: UnregisterGrainForTesting
methods.description: Unregisters a grain for testing purposes, returning 1 if successful, 0 if not found.

methods.name: GetOrCreateActivation
methods.description: Retrieves an existing activation or creates a new one, handling rehydration and activation asynchronously.

methods.name: UnregisterNonExistentActivation
methods.description: Asynchronously unregisters a non-existent activation from the grain locator.

methods.name: TryGetGrainContext
methods.description: Attempts to retrieve runtime data for a specific grain activation.

methods.name: DeactivateActivations
methods.description: Gracefully deactivates a list of activations, waiting for completion.

methods.name: DeactivateAllActivations
methods.description: Deactivates all activations in the directory, typically during shutdown.

methods.name: DeleteActivations
methods.description: Deletes specified activations based on their addresses.

methods.name: OnSiloStatusChange
methods.description: Handles changes in silo status, deactivating activations if a silo becomes unavailable or fails.

methods.name: Participate
methods.description: Participates in the silo lifecycle, primarily to ensure the catalog registers itself in the activation directory.
